run_query.description: Run a query written in OpenAlex Query Language, which reads like a sentence: 'works where year is (2020) and cited_by_count > (100) group by type'. OQL reaches questions the filter fields cannot express - nested boolean logic, proximity search, grouping written into the query itself - and the query names its own entity, so one action covers every kind. The query object form takes the same query as JSON, which is easier to build from a program. Sent as a POST, so a systematic-review query too long for a URL still works. Every result echoes your query back in all three spellings.

search_works.description: Search and filter OpenAlex's catalogue of scholarly works: journal articles, preprints, books, datasets, dissertations and more. Search the title, abstract and full text by keyword or by meaning, then narrow by publication date, work type, open-access status, language, author, institution, country, journal, topic, funder, UN Sustainable Development Goal, licence or citation count. Sort by citations or date, page through any number of results, take a random sample, or turn the whole thing into counts with 'Count by' - works per year, per country, per journal.

results.abstract: Despite growing interest in Open Access (OA) to scholarly literature, there is an unmet need for large-scale, up-to-date, and reproducible studies assessing the prevalence and characteristics of OA.

translate_query.description: Translate a query between the three ways OpenAlex spells one - readable OQL, a JSON query object, and a classic /works?filter=... URL - and validate it, without running it. An invalid query comes back with the character position and a suggested fix rather than a silent empty result. Costs nothing at all, so it is the cheap check before spending credits, and the way to turn a URL somebody sent you into something readable.
